A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BIOMEDICA research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete supplementary material support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification and retrieval experiments, base-model screening, dataset statistics, and annotation-agreement analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results, including performance Tables 2–4 and supplementary base-model and annotation analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 revises the stated label-resolution rule from re-evaluating tied votes to reviewing concepts identified by only one annotator. The clustering pipeline, encoders, continual-pretraining variants, and model merging remain unchanged; the model renaming and newly named contrastive loss do not establish additional method changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same biomedical archive, 39 classification tasks, and approximately 7K-pair Flickr retrieval benchmark. The full appendix taxonomy and benchmark provenance table are unchanged; revised taxonomy summary counts do not establish different data or task coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain OpenCLIP, CoCa, PMC-CLIP, BioMedCLIP, and the same proposed-model variants; base-model screening also retains its comparators. V3 deletes the prose mention of training from scratch, but no separately identified comparator result disappears.

E3.justification: Section 14.2 revises the stated annotation-time target used to select 2,000 clusters from at most 72 to 48 hours per annotator. Training hyperparameters, evaluation tasks, metrics, and testing procedures otherwise match. This reported budget revision does not establish that annotation or experiments were repeated.

E4.justification: The filtering, balancing, full-data, and WiSE-FT comparisons remain, together with base-model screening, PCA analysis, and annotation-disagreement analysis. Figure 3 redisplays dataset composition without introducing a new analytical question or robustness experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 95% confidence intervals using SciPy nonparametric bootstrapping with 1,000 resamples and default settings. Seed information, repeated-run reporting, and annotation-disagreement statistics are unchanged.

E6.justification: Section 4 changes the reported taxonomy size from 12 global and 170 local concepts to 16 and 119, matching the hierarchy already present in both appendices. It also removes several earlier taxonomy-count statements and revises Figure 3's composition display. Classification, retrieval, and base-model screening scores are numerically identical.

T1.justification: The classification-to-text formulation, embedding-similarity prediction rule, and retrieval equations are unchanged in the evaluation appendix. No mathematical assumptions, proofs, theorems, or substantive derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the large open biomedical archive, expert-guided metadata, streamed continual CLIP pretraining, and broad zero-shot evaluation. The abstract and conclusion retain the same performance and compute-efficiency claims.

C2.justification: Section 7 adds an interpretation linking filtering gains to alignment between pretraining data and evaluation domains, supported by a DataComp comparison. Section 5 removes the explanation that PMC-15M's unavailability motivated the Flickr benchmark. The context-length and image-resizing limitations remain.

D1.justification: V3 explicitly identifies the contrastive loss and clarifies local-topic balancing, but removes the July–September 2024 download window, exact balanced and filtered subset sizes, and the unweighted-averaging disclosure. Hyperparameter tables, hardware descriptions, and code/data access links remain. Rounded subset sizes do not establish changed training data.

R1.justification: V3 adds references to MicroVQA, DataComp, and contrastive predictive coding, including a new connection between its filtering findings and DataComp. The broader positioning relative to existing biomedical datasets and contrastive models remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 standardizes BMCA-CLIP/BMCA-LIP to BMC-CLIP, edits and condenses passages, rebuilds the supplementary contents list, and moves acknowledgments into the supplement. These are limited editorial and organizational revisions within the retained narrative.

P2.justification: Figure 3 replaces the nested pie with separate panel-type and global-concept pies and revises its legend and word cloud; Figure 4 gains shaded polygons. The metadata table moves to the supplement, the microscopy-results table is repositioned, and the author block and supplementary numbering are reformatted.

improvement.justification: V3 modestly improves clarity and correctness through a more accurate supplementary contents list, clearer visual organization, and main-text taxonomy counts that match the unchanged appendix hierarchy. These gains are limited by omitted reproducibility details and conflicting counts still retained in Table S1 and Figure 2. The experimental evidence itself is unchanged.
